subject: Bifactor model with categorical data: Convergence issue

messages.author: 6e1c0d1ed0801c3e
messages.subject: Bifactor model with categorical data: Convergence issue
parts:
Hello,

I have categorical (binary) data, and I'm attempting to run a CFA on 132 items, with 1483 observations. I initially specified a bifactor model with 132 items loading onto one factor, and each item loading onto one of six specific factors (with roughly equal numbers of items per factor). Below is my code (note that given the number of items I have, the "model specification" part is abridged):

Model specification
general.factor =~
Nat_Corr_4_AN_0028_01_hf050 + 
Nat_Corr_11_AN_0104_03_hf040 +  
Nat_Corr_13_AN_1237_01_hf012 +
Nat_Corr_24_AN_1242_01_hf028 +
Nat_Corr_25_AN_0542_01_hf015 +
... (and so on for 132 items)

factor.1 =~ 22 items
factor.2 =~ 22 items
factor.3 =~ 22 items
factor.4 =~ 22 items
factor.5 =~ 22 items
factor.6 =~ 22 items

Running the CFA
mod.bifactor <- cfa(bifactor.model, data = df.newstudy, ordered = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE, estimator = "WLSMV") 

Below is the error I get when I run this model, and I can't get any fit measures or parameter estimates (any attempt to do so brings up a message telling me the model didn't converge):

lavaan WARNING: the optimizer (NLMINB) claimed the model converged,
                  but not all elements of the gradient are (near) zero;
                  the optimizer may not have found a local solution
                  use check.gradient = FALSE to skip this check.

I noticed that I get the same error when I specify a unidimensional model with all 132 items loading onto one factor. This error does not occur when I run a six-factor model with only the specific factors, so it looks like there's some sort of issue with that more general factor.

I found a previous post where someone had the same error, and the advice given was to look at potential model identification issues--but I don't think the model is underidentified. Is there anything about categorical data/use of polychoric correlations that inflates the likelihood of nonconvergence?

Please let me know if any additional information is required. Thanks!

Louisa
